[&_blockquote_p::after]:hidden","children":[["$","h1","h1-0",{"children":"Celia Cruz"}],"\n",["$","h3","h3-0",{"children":"Early Life and Musical Beginnings"}],"\n",["$","p","p-0",{"children":"Celia Cruz (1925–2003) was a legendary Cuban-American singer celebrated internationally as the \"Queen of Salsa.\" Over a career spanning six decades, she became a global icon of Latin music, known for her powerful voice, rhythmic style, and signature catchphrase, \"¡Azúcar!\" She was born Úrsula Hilaria Celia de la Caridad Cruz Alfonso on October 21, 1925, in the Santos Suárez neighborhood of Havana, Cuba. Raised in a working-class family, her musical talent was evident from a young age. She began her career in the 1940s and 1950s in Cuba, winning radio contests and performing in local cabarets, slowly building a reputation for her unmistakable voice and charismatic stage presence."}],"\n",["$","h3","h3-1",{"children":"Rise to Prominence in Cuba"}],"\n",["$","p","p-1",{"children":["Cruz gained significant prominence in 1950 when she became the lead vocalist for the renowned orchestra La Sonora Matancera. This collaboration propelled her to stardom across Latin America, earning her the nickname ",["$","em","em-0",{"children":"La Guarachera de Cuba"}],". Her time with La Sonora Matancera allowed her to refine her craft, blending traditional Afro-Cuban rhythms with modern orchestrations. During this period, she recorded numerous hits and toured extensively, solidifying her status as a premier vocalist in the vibrant Cuban music scene of the 1950s."]}],"\n",["$","p","p-2",{"children":["$","img","img-0",{"src":"https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5a/Celia_Cruz_1950s.jpg","alt":"Celia Cruz Performing"}]}],"\n",["$","blockquote","blockquote-0",{"children":["\n",["$","p","p-0",{"children":"\"Singing is my life. It has always been my life. It will always be my life.\""}],"\n"]}],"\n",["$","h3","h3-2",{"children":"Exile and the Birth of Salsa"}],"\n",["$","p","p-3",{"children":"Following the Cuban Revolution and the rise of Fidel Castro, Cruz's life changed dramatically. In 1960, while on tour in Mexico, she and the band defected, eventually settling in the United States. She would never return to her homeland, a profound sorrow that she carried throughout her life and which deeply influenced her music."}],"\n","$L8","\n","$L9","\n","$La","\n","$Lb","\n","$Lc","\n","$Ld"]}]]}],"$Le","$Lf",false]}],"$L10"]}]

8:["$","p","p-4",{"children":"In the U.S., particularly in New York City, Cruz became a pivotal figure in the creation and popularization of the \"salsa\" genre in the 1960s and 1970s. She collaborated with iconic artists such as Tito Puente, Johnny Pacheco, and the Fania All-Stars. These collaborations helped define the salsa sound—a dynamic fusion of Cuban son, mambo, jazz, and other Latin and Caribbean rhythms. Her energetic performances, elaborate costumes, and rhythmic mastery made her the undisputed Queen of Salsa."}]
9:["$","h3","h3-3",{"children":"Global Stardom and Legacy"}]
a:["$","p","p-5",{"children":"Throughout her illustrious career, Cruz recorded over 70 albums, earned numerous gold and platinum records, and won three Grammy Awards and four Latin Grammy Awards. Some of her most famous songs, including \"La Vida es un Carnaval,\" \"Quimbara,\" and \"Bemba Colorá,\" remain anthems of Latin culture worldwide."}]
b:["$","p","p-6",{"children":"Beyond her musical achievements, Cruz was a cultural ambassador and a symbol of resilience for the Cuban diaspora. Her catchphrase, \"¡Azúcar!\" (Sugar!), originally a spontaneous call during a performance, became a universal declaration of joy, energy, and Afro-Cuban heritage."}]
c:["$","p","p-7",{"children":"Celia Cruz passed away in New Jersey on July 16, 2003, at the age of 77. Her death was mourned globally, with massive public viewings in Miami and New York. She remains one of the most influential figures in Afro-Cuban and Latin music history, her legacy living on through her timeless recordings and the countless artists she inspired."}]
